item.title: Macron urges Iran to negotiate in third call with Pezeshkian since war began
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron called on Iran to cease its "unacceptable attacks" on countries across the Middle East and engage in good-faith negotiations during a phone call with Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian on Tuesday, according to an AFP dispatch and Macron's own posts on X. The call marked Macron's third conversation with Pezeshkian since the United States and Israel launched military operations against Iran on February 28, following earlier calls on March 8 and March 15.

item.title: Lebanon expels Iran's ambassador as Israel vows to occupy southern Lebanon
item.description: Israeli Defense Minister Israel Katz announced on Tuesday that the military plans to occupy southern Lebanon up to the Litani River, marking the clearest indication yet that Israel intends to seize and hold territory amounting to nearly a tenth of Lebanon as its campaign against Hezbollah deepens. The declaration came alongside a dramatic diplomatic rupture between Lebanon and Iran, with Beirut expelling Tehran's ambassador over the role it says Iran played in dragging the country into war.

item.title: China presses Iran to start peace talks as Gulf war escalates
item.description:
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi called his Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi on Tuesday, pressing Tehran to seize "every opportunity and window for peace" and begin negotiations to end the war that has engulfed the Middle East since late February. "Talking is always better than to keep fighting," Wang told Araghchi, according to a Chinese foreign ministry statement, adding that "all hotspot issues should be resolved through dialogue and negotiation, not by using force."

The call, held at Iran's request according to Beijing, comes at a delicate moment. President Donald Trump claimed Monday that the United States had held "very good and productive conversations" with a "top person" in Iran's leadership, and extended by five days a deadline to strike the country's power plants to allow for talks. Tehran has flatly denied any direct negotiations are taking place, with parliamentary speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf accusing Trump of seeking "to manipulate the financial and oil markets."

item.title: Kuwait destroys 13 missiles, 10 drones as Iran strikes Gulf states
item.description: Kuwait's air defense systems intercepted a barrage of Iranian ballistic missiles and drones early Tuesday, with falling debris damaging homes and knocking out power lines across parts of the country, the Defense Ministry said. No casualties were reported.

item.title: Drone strike hits Kuwait airport fuel tank, no casualties reported
item.description: A drone attack struck a fuel tank at Kuwait International Airport on Tuesday, igniting a fire but causing no casualties, according to Kuwait's civil aviation authority. The strike is the latest in a series of Iranian retaliatory attacks on Gulf state infrastructure that have repeatedly targeted the airport since late February.

item.title: British troops down 14 drones in record night at Iraq base
item.description: British forces stationed in northern Iraq shot down 14 Iranian "kamikaze" drones overnight on Monday, the Ministry of Defence confirmed on Tuesday, marking the highest number of unmanned aerial vehicles destroyed in a single night since the US-Israeli military campaign against Iran began nearly four weeks ago.

item.title: Debris from intercepted missiles knocks out 7 Kuwait power lines
item.description:
Kuwait's electricity grid suffered fresh damage on Tuesday after falling debris from intercepted Iranian missiles and drones knocked seven overhead power transmission lines out of service, triggering partial blackouts across several parts of the country.

The Ministry of Electricity, Water, and Renewable Energy confirmed the disruptions late Monday, with spokesperson Eng. Fatima Jawhar Hayat saying the damage resulted from air defense interception activities, according to a statement carried by Kuwait's state news agency KUNA. Technical teams were mobilized but could not begin full assessments until security authorities cleared the affected sites.

item.title: Iran says drones struck Israeli defense sites, Ben Gurion Airport
item.description: Iran's armed forces said on Tuesday that they carried out a series of drone strikes targeting Israeli defense industry facilities and military infrastructure at Ben Gurion Airport, marking the latest escalation in a conflict now in its fourth week.

item.title: Iranian missile intercepted over Lebanon in first since regional war began
item.description: An Iranian ballistic missile was intercepted over Lebanese airspace on Tuesday in what security officials described as the first such incident since the regional war began, sending debris raining down on communities north of Beirut and deepening fears that Lebanon is being drawn further into the expanding conflict between Iran and Israel.

item.title: Death toll rises to 69 in Colombia military plane crash
item.description: A Colombian Air Force C-130 Hercules transport plane crashed into dense jungle shortly after takeoff on Monday, killing 69 members of the country's security forces in one of the deadliest air disasters in Colombian military history. The death toll, updated Tuesday by the armed forces, also left 57 people injured and one still missing.

item.title: Denmark's left bloc wins election but falls short of majority
item.description:
Denmark's left-wing bloc led by Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen emerged ahead in Tuesday's parliamentary election but failed to secure a governing majority, with the Social Democrats posting their weakest result in 125 years and leaving centrist Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen positioned as kingmaker in what promises to be weeks of coalition negotiations.

With nearly all votes counted late Tuesday, the "red bloc" of left-leaning parties captured 84 seats in Denmark's 179-seat Folketing, while the right-wing "blue bloc" secured 77 seats — both well short of the 90 needed for a majority. Rasmussen's centrist Moderates, which won 14 seats, now hold the balance of power.

item.title: Iran refuses talks with Witkoff and Kushner, eyes Vance
item.description:
Iran has refused to continue diplomatic engagement with President Donald Trump's top envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, accusing them of deception in the lead-up to the U.S.-Israeli strikes that began on February 28, according to The Telegraph. Gulf sources told the publication that Tehran now views Vice President JD Vance as its preferred American interlocutor, owing to his well-documented skepticism of military intervention abroad.

The shift comes as mediating nations work to arrange a potential meeting in Islamabad, Pakistan, that could bring together Vance and Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf as early as this week.

item.title: Trump claims Iran gave US an energy 'present' tied to Hormuz
item.description:
President Donald Trump said on Tuesday that Iran had made a major energy-related concession to the United States, describing it as a gift that "arrived today" — though he offered no specifics and Iran has repeatedly denied engaging in any negotiations with Washington.

"They gave us a present and the present arrived today, and it was a very big present, worth a tremendous amount of money," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office, according to Reuters. "It wasn't nuclear; it was oil-and-gas-related, and it was a very nice thing they did."

Trump said the gesture was connected to the Strait of Hormuz, the critical waterway through which roughly 20% of the world's oil supply passes. He characterized it as proof that "we're dealing with the right people" in Tehran and claimed Iran had also agreed it "will never have a nuclear weapon," The Independent reported.

item.title: Netanyahu taps top aide Dermer to vet US-Iran deal
item.description:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu assigned his closest confidant, former Strategic Affairs Minister Ron Dermer, to monitor US-Iranian negotiations and ensure Israel's core interests are not sacrificed in any potential deal to end the war, according to Bloomberg, citing an Israeli official speaking on condition of anonymity.

Dermer's primary focus is on ensuring the dismantlement of Iran's nuclear program and the removal and elimination of roughly 440 kilograms of highly enriched uranium — material that Iran reportedly boasted to White House Special Envoy Steve Witkoff was sufficient for 11 nuclear bombs, according to Jewish Insider.

item.title: US airstrikes kill 15 Iraq PMF fighters, including Anbar commander
item.description:
Airstrikes attributed to the United States and Israel killed at least 15 fighters from Iraq's Popular Mobilization Forces and wounded 30 others in western Iraq early Tuesday, in the deadliest single attack on the Iran-backed militia coalition since the US-Israeli war on Iran began in late February.

The strikes hit a PMF command headquarters in Iraq's Anbar province during a security meeting attended by senior commanders, according to Reuters. Among the dead was Saad al-Baiji, the PMF's operations commander for Anbar province. The PMF confirmed his death along with 14 of his companions in a statement posted on social media, calling the attack "a treacherous American targeting that struck the operations headquarters".

item.title: Iran charges ships up to $2M for Hormuz passage
item.description:
Iran has begun levying transit fees of up to $2 million per voyage on some commercial vessels passing through the Strait of Hormuz, effectively creating an informal toll on the world's most critical maritime energy chokepoint, according to Bloomberg.

The payments are being sought on an ad hoc basis and do not appear to be systematic, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg. Some ships have already made the payment, though the mechanism and currency used remain unclear. Iranian authorities have officially denied that a formal policy exists, calling the reports "unfounded".

item.title: Israeli airstrike hits Christian town north of Beirut for first time
item.description:
An Israeli airstrike struck the Christian town of Sahel Alma north of Beirut on Tuesday, marking the first time the area had been targeted in the expanding war between Israel and Hezbollah, according to Lebanese state media and Reuters. There were no immediate reports of casualties, but witnesses told Reuters they heard several blasts and saw white smoke rising from the town.

The strike represents a widening of Israel's air campaign into areas previously untouched by the conflict, which has killed more than 1,000 people in Lebanon and displaced over one million since fighting escalated on March 2.

item.title: Oil drops as US sends Iran 15-point ceasefire proposal
item.description: Oil prices swung sharply on Monday and Tuesday as reports emerged that the United States had sent Iran a 15-point proposal to end the war now in its fourth week, offering a potential off-ramp from a conflict that has roiled global energy markets and sent American gas prices soaring.

item.title: Brazil court places Bolsonaro under house arrest on health grounds
item.description:
Brazilian Supreme Court Justice Alexandre de Moraes ruled on Tuesday to place former President Jair Bolsonaro under house arrest on health grounds, reversing months of denied requests from the right-wing leader's legal team, according to Reuters.

Bolsonaro, 71, has been serving a 27-year prison sentence since November for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election to President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva. The house arrest will last for an initial 90-day period, after which Moraes said conditions will be reassessed. "The presence of the requirements necessary for maintaining humanitarian house arrest will be reassessed, including a medical examination if needed," the justice wrote in the decision.

item.title: Astronomers spot two planets forming around a young star like our sun
item.description: An international team of astronomers has confirmed the discovery of a second planet forming in the dust disk surrounding the young star WISPIT 2, making it only the second known system where two planets have been directly observed taking shape around their host star. The findings, published Tuesday in The Astrophysical Journal Letters, offer what researchers describe as the closest analog yet to our own solar system in its infancy.
